name: M5StackChan AI Desktop Robot
description: M5Stack's preassembled AI desktop companion built on the ESP32-S3-based CoreS3 controller — a pan/tilt face display with camera and voice interaction, co-created with the open-source Stack-chan community project. Factory firmware can be replaced with community alternatives over USB.

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: fully local option; StackChan World app optional for setup

sourcing: Specs sourced from M5Stack's official StackChan product page and m5-docs hardware reference, plus the stack-chan/stack-chan and andymai/stackchan-kai GitHub repositories, as of September 2026. The exact open-source license for the official firmware could not be confirmed from the pages checked. robotindex does not sell this product — pricing shown is for reference and may vary by retailer.

pricing.summary: **$99.00** for the assembled StackChan unit with CoreS3 pre-installed, per M5Stack's official store. Includes a 50cm USB-A-to-USB-C cable, a character expression sticker, a printed manual, and a carrying case.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: Built around M5Stack's CoreS3 development module (ESP32-S3), StackChan pairs a 2.0" capacitive touchscreen — used as an animated face — with a two-servo pan/tilt base giving 360° continuous horizontal rotation and 90° of vertical head movement. A front-facing GC0308 camera and dual microphones (ES7210 codec) support the factory AI Agent's voice interaction and a companion mobile app, while a 9-axis IMU (BMI270 + BMM150), NFC reader, and proximity/ambient-light sensor round out the sensor package. A 1W speaker with a 16-bit I2S amplifier handles audio output, and the whole unit runs on a 550 mAh internal battery.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: No recalls, lawsuits, safety incidents, or data-privacy reports were found for the M5StackChan in the sources reviewed here.
